### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. severe combined immunodeficiency due to IKK2 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.484)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1169091, Reactome:R-HSA-202424, Reactome:R-HSA-2871837, Reactome:R-HSA-5607764)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in MALT1 (None) —DISRUPTS→ MALT1 (HGNC:6870); MALT1 (HGNC:6870) —DECREASES→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP435); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP435) —DECREASES→ Abnormal B cell differentiation (HP:0003304); Abnormal B cell differentiation (HP:0003304) —LEADS_TO→ Severe combined immunodeficiency (HP:0001844); Pathogenic variant in IKBKB (None) —DISRUPTS→ IKBKB (HGNC:5566); IKBKB (HGNC:5566) —DECREASES→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP435). Loss-of-function variants in MALT1 (Disease A) and IKBKB (Disease B, encoding IKK2) both lead to impaired activation of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. This impairment disrupts normal B cell differentiation, contributing to the immunodeficiency seen in both conditions, though the specific manifestations differ.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in MALT1 are found to cause a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, or if IKBKB variants in Disease B are not loss-of-function, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, if mutations in MALT1 do not impact the NF-kappaB pathway, or if mutations in IKBKB do not impact the NF-kappaB pathway, this would falsify the proposed link. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD in the coding regions of MALT1 or IKBKB that are implicated in these diseases would weaken the hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the NF-kappaB pathway in these distinct but related immunodeficiencies could inform therapeutic strategies. Modulating NF-kappaB signaling or downstream effectors might offer a common therapeutic avenue for patients with defects in either MALT1 or IKBKB.
